channel.title: EXPLORING KOREAN LITERATURE A
channel.desc:
2021 Exploring Korean Literature There is a growing interest in Korean literature among readers from around the world and so we bring Korean classics to Korean modern literature to viewers in this special series under three themes. What They?ve Read Well-known TV personalities read three translated works of Korean literature that have recently received attention. Kim Soom's novel \"One Left\", brings the comfort women issue to the forefront of the literary world, and her book is recited and discussed by Darcy Paquet, a translator and essayist for the film \"Parasite,\" and translator and essayist Colin Marshall, Italian architect Simone Carena, and fashion designer Shin Ji-hye. The novel was published in the U.S. in September 2020 and a second book print was released this year. Cho Nam-Joo's novel \"Kim Jiyoung, Born 1982\" has been translated into 25 languages and is recited by TV personality Daniel Hicks (UK), Carlos Gorito (Brazil), YouTuber Sarah Mack (USA) and singer Punita (India) who share their thoughts about the book. Howon, a member of the boy band, W24, recites passages from Kim Young-ha's novel \"Diary of a Murderer\" and gives commentary. Living to Tell a Story This documentary features Korean writers whose works are not only popular in Korea but also overseas. In episode 1, poet Kim Yi-deum, the Winner of the National Translation Award and the Lucien Stryk Award for her collection of poems, \"Hysteria,\" as well as Korean novelists Kim Cho-Yup and Kim Yeon-su appear to talk about the creative process and how they carry out research before writing a novel. In Episode 2, novelist Yun Ko-Eun, the winner of the Crime Fiction in Translation Dagger award for her book, \"The Disaster Tourist\", and novelist Ha Seong-nan and poet Jin Eun-young explain what they were trying to convey to readers through their works. In Episode 3, novelist Hwang Sok-young, whose works are mostly inspired by his own experience of living in modern Korean society, tells the story of his life and literary journey. A Word Depicted in Stories The cultural characteristics in Korean literature that encompasses Korean classics to modern novels are highlighted on this show. Six episodes with different themes ranging from female poets in classical literature, makeup culture, wine and arts, tea ceremony, pets, and a literary discussion forum will begin airing on November 5th. -->

channel.name: Arirang World KR
channel.title: EXPLORING KOREAN LITERATURE B
channel.desc:
2021 Exploring Korean Literature There is a growing interest in Korean literature among readers from around the world and so we bring Korean classics to Korean modern literature to viewers in this special series under three themes. What They?ve Read Well-known TV personalities read three translated works of Korean literature that have recently received attention. Kim Soom's novel \"One Left\", brings the comfort women issue to the forefront of the literary world, and her book is recited and discussed by Darcy Paquet, a translator and essayist for the film \"Parasite,\" and translator and essayist Colin Marshall, Italian architect Simone Carena, and fashion designer Shin Ji-hye. The novel was published in the U.S. in September 2020 and a second book print was released this year. Cho Nam-Joo's novel \"Kim Jiyoung, Born 1982\" has been translated into 25 languages and is recited by TV personality Daniel Hicks (UK), Carlos Gorito (Brazil), YouTuber Sarah Mack (USA) and singer Punita (India) who share their thoughts about the book. Howon, a member of the boy band, W24, recites passages from Kim Young-ha's novel \"Diary of a Murderer\" and gives commentary. Living to Tell a Story This documentary features Korean writers whose works are not only popular in Korea but also overseas. In episode 1, poet Kim Yi-deum, the Winner of the National Translation Award and the Lucien Stryk Award for her collection of poems, \"Hysteria,\" as well as Korean novelists Kim Cho-Yup and Kim Yeon-su appear to talk about the creative process and how they carry out research before writing a novel. In Episode 2, novelist Yun Ko-Eun, the winner of the Crime Fiction in Translation Dagger award for her book, \"The Disaster Tourist\", and novelist Ha Seong-nan and poet Jin Eun-young explain what they were trying to convey to readers through their works. In Episode 3, novelist Hwang Sok-young, whose works are mostly inspired by his own experience of living in modern Korean society, tells the story of his life and literary journey. A Word Depicted in Stories The cultural characteristics in Korean literature that encompasses Korean classics to modern novels are highlighted on this show. Six episodes with different themes ranging from female poets in classical literature, makeup culture, wine and arts, tea ceremony, pets, and a literary discussion forum will begin airing on November 5th. -->

Episode 4: Korean Language Connecting the World Witness how Korean has grown into a global language of culture, creativity, and connection ? a bridge linking people across nations.\"Sponsored by King Sejong Institute Foundation\".

channel.name: Arirang World KR
channel.title: EXPLORING KOREAN LITERATURE A
channel.desc:
2021 Exploring Korean Literature There is a growing interest in Korean literature among readers from around the world and so we bring Korean classics to Korean modern literature to viewers in this special series under three themes. What They?ve Read Well-known TV personalities read three translated works of Korean literature that have recently received attention. Kim Soom's novel \"One Left\", brings the comfort women issue to the forefront of the literary world, and her book is recited and discussed by Darcy Paquet, a translator and essayist for the film \"Parasite,\" and translator and essayist Colin Marshall, Italian architect Simone Carena, and fashion designer Shin Ji-hye. The novel was published in the U.S. in September 2020 and a second book print was released this year. Cho Nam-Joo's novel \"Kim Jiyoung, Born 1982\" has been translated into 25 languages and is recited by TV personality Daniel Hicks (UK), Carlos Gorito (Brazil), YouTuber Sarah Mack (USA) and singer Punita (India) who share their thoughts about the book. Howon, a member of the boy band, W24, recites passages from Kim Young-ha's novel \"Diary of a Murderer\" and gives commentary. Living to Tell a Story This documentary features Korean writers whose works are not only popular in Korea but also overseas. In episode 1, poet Kim Yi-deum, the Winner of the National Translation Award and the Lucien Stryk Award for her collection of poems, \"Hysteria,\" as well as Korean novelists Kim Cho-Yup and Kim Yeon-su appear to talk about the creative process and how they carry out research before writing a novel. In Episode 2, novelist Yun Ko-Eun, the winner of the Crime Fiction in Translation Dagger award for her book, \"The Disaster Tourist\", and novelist Ha Seong-nan and poet Jin Eun-young explain what they were trying to convey to readers through their works. In Episode 3, novelist Hwang Sok-young, whose works are mostly inspired by his own experience of living in modern Korean society, tells the story of his life and literary journey. A Word Depicted in Stories The cultural characteristics in Korean literature that encompasses Korean classics to modern novels are highlighted on this show. Six episodes with different themes ranging from female poets in classical literature, makeup culture, wine and arts, tea ceremony, pets, and a literary discussion forum will begin airing on November 5th. -->
.

channel.desc: As of April 2025, S. Korea has established diplomatic relations with a total of 194 countries. Among them are countries that have had ties and exchanges with Korea for hundreds of years. With such long-standing relationships with so many nations, might there be fascinating hidden stories between Korea and the rest of the world that we don?t know yet? \"Diplomat?s Archives: Hidden Stories\" begins with this very question. Together with foreign embassies in Korea, the series uncovers and sheds light on meaningful yet lesser-known stories between Korea and other countries. Through this, we aim to reaffirm the deep friendships that have been built over time, highlight how countries are interconnected?bilaterally and multilaterally? and emphasize the importance of cooperation on the global stage today.

channel.title: DIVE INTO KOREAN
channel.desc: ?Dive into Korean? is an introductory educational documentary series designed for learners beginning their journey with the Korean language. The program explores the historical and cultural essence of Hangeul, the Korean alphabet, and the spirit behind its creation by King Sejong the Great. Through engaging storytelling and real-life experiences, the series helps viewers understand the beauty, science, and philosophy embedded in the Korean language. Episode 1: Hangeul ? A Script Anyone Can Learn Easily Discover how Hangeul was designed as an easy and logical writing system for all people, embodying King Sejong?s vision of communication and equality. Episode 2: Hangeul ? A Script That Illustrates the Sounds of Speech Explore the scientific principles behind Hangeul?s creation ? how its characters visually represent the shape and movement of the human speech organs. Episode 3: The More You Know the Culture, the Closer You Get to Korean Understand how culture and language intertwine, and how learning about Korean traditions and expressions brings learners closer to authentic communication. Episode 4: Korean Language Connecting the World Witness how Korean has grown into a global language of culture, creativity, and connection ? a bridge linking people across nations.\"Sponsored by King Sejong Institute Foundation\".

channel.name: BBC Two NL
channel.title: Natural World
channel.desc: Biologist Joe Hutto was mother to the strangest family in the world, 13 endangered wild turkeys that he raised from their eggs. For a whole year his turkey children were his only companions as he walked them deep through the Florida Everglades. Suffering all the heartache and joy of any other parent as he raised his new family, he even learnt to speak their language and began to see the world through turkey eyes.

channel.desc: Forced out of Crystal City, a group of Mormons head westward in search of the promised land. The journey is treacherous, and two footloose horse traders are persuaded to give the Lord a hand and guide them across the desert. On the trail, the wagon train encounters travelling entertainers, fugitive gunfighters and Indians in this poetic observation of the lives of these pioneering people.

channel.name: BBC Two NL

The second in John Ford's cavalry trilogy, the film produced an Oscar for Winton C Hoch's cinematography and one of John Wayne's finest performances - as a man learning to accept the relentless march of time.

Performances from big-hitter soloists Phil Collins, Shakin' Stevens and Kim Wilde are featured alongside the exuberant chaos of groups like Tenpole Tudor, Adam and the Ants and the Teardrop Explodes.

channel.name: BBC Two NL
channel.title: Top of the Pops

The show embraces the shift with a new theme tune and titles and, as Legs and Co leave, invite a swathe of club kids and cheerleaders in to create a permanent 80s party atmosphere.

channel.name: BBC Two NL
channel.title: Top of the Pops

channel.title: Book TV
channel.desc: This long-running staple of the C-SPAN2 weekend schedule helps expand the channel's programming beyond politics. Most episodes of "Book TV" feature discussions with authors of nonfiction books, usually in the form of interviews, lectures or seminars. The series sometimes includes coverage of major book fairs and festivals. Some of the notable names who have appeared on the show include David Mamet and Tom Clancy.

channel.title: Nobuyuki Tsujii al Carnegie Hall
channel.desc: Sonata per pianoforte n.17 in re minore detta La tempesta, op.31 n.2, composta da Beethoven nel 1802 - Nobuyuki Tsujii, pianoforte \(New York, Carnegie Hall - 2012\).

channel.name: Classica IT
channel.title: Speciale Almanacco - Pugile e Vittoria
channel.desc: Puntata speciale di Almanacco di Bellezza dedicata alla mostra Il Pugile e la Vittoria, esposizione di due bronzi di eta' ellenistica e romana presso il parco archeologico di Brescia - con P.Maranghi, L.Piccinini \(2023\).

channel.name: Classica IT
channel.title: Beethoven - Quartetto op.59 n.2

channel.name: Classica IT
channel.title: Brahms - Un Requiem tedesco
channel.desc: Requiem non liturgico composto nel 1868. L'idea originaria si fa risalire alla morte dell'amico R.Schumann - con G.Kuehmeier, G.Finley - Coro Radio Olandese - Concertgebouw Orchestra - M.Jansons, dir. \(Amsterdam, 2012\).

channel.name: Classica IT
channel.title: Almanacco di Bellezza
channel.desc: Piero Maranghi, direttore di Classica HD, passa in rassegna, anniversari e ricorrenze legati la mondo dell'arte, della cultura, della storia e dello sport. In studio con lui, il collezionista ed esperto d'arte Leonardo Piccinini.

channel.name: Classica IT
channel.title: Anna Netrebko e Yusif Eyvazov - Parte 1
channel.desc: Verdi, Puccini, Mascagni, Ponchielli: un grande concerto delle piu' celebri arie e duetti d'opera - Hungarian State Opera Orchestra - Neuer Kammerchor Potsdam - Michelangelo Mazza, dir. \(Waldbuhne, Berlino - 2017\).

channel.name: Classica IT
channel.title: Prokof'ev - Matrimonio al convento
channel.desc: Opera lirico-comica \(1940\) in quattro atti su libretto di Prokof'ev e Mira Mendelson - con L.Diadkova, N.Gassiev - Orchestra del Teatro Mariinskij-Opera Kirov - V.Gergiev, dir. - V.Pazi, reg. \(San Pietroburgo, 1997\).

channel.name: Classica IT
channel.title: Mestiere Teatro
channel.desc: Un viaggio alla scoperta di quanti nei teatri, lontano dalla ribalta, in ufficio, nei laboratori, dietro le quinte, nella buca, lavorano per la riuscita e il successo di uno spettacolo. A cura di Paolo Gavazzeni.

channel.name: Classica IT
channel.title: Incontri contemporanei - Del Corno
channel.desc: Protagonista della puntata e' il compositore milanese Filippo Del Corno \(classe 1970\), autore dell'opera Non guardate al domani sull'assassinio di Aldo Moro e autore affermato anche all'estero - a cura di A.Daveri \(2009\).

channel.name: Classica IT
channel.title: La Classica domanda - Nicola Piovani
channel.desc: Proseguono le interviste a cura di Anton Giulio Onofri a personalita' del mondo della cultura e dello spettacolo. Ospite della Classica domanda di oggi e' il pianista e compositore Nicola Piovani \(2014\).

channel.name: Classica IT
channel.title: Beethoven - Sinfonia n.6

channel.name: NHK World JP
channel.title: Darwin's Amazing Animals
channel.desc: Japanese pond turtles live in the rivers and ponds of Japan. Recently, however, the species has been designated as near threatened due to environmental changes and the presence of invasive species. However, during a six-month tracking project, researchers found that they actually take full advantage of the rich Satoyama landscape areas. They feed on insects in rice paddies, fruits in the woods and tomatoes in the fields. The team also discovered that they even lay eggs in agricultural greenhouses. This episode looks through the eyes of these amazing creatures to reveal their surprising way of life.

channel.name: NHK World JP
channel.title: Easy Japanese For Work
channel.desc: Today: determining what is worrying a client. Lin Zhipeng, from China, works at a real estate firm. He began studying Japanese after becoming interested in anime, and came to Japan five years ago. At his job, he's involved with property inspections and assisting clients. He had a bad experience once when a customer asked to change to a Japanese agent. He wants to regain his confidence. In a roleplay challenge, he must determine what is worrying his client.

channel.name: NHK World JP
channel.title: Zero Waste Life
channel.desc: Lumber that's too short or too narrow can be hard to sell. Offcuts are usually discarded or end up as woodchips. But Tanaka Ryosuke and Miyachi Yoh use them for furniture. Not big enough for large panels, multiple boards must be glued together, leading to uneven coloring. The answer, to dye the furniture with indigo, transforming each piece into a unified whole. This clever idea and their love of wood itself gives their work an inner beauty that's attracting real interest.

channel.desc: Long-running sitcom "The Adventures of Ozzie and Harriet," based on a radio show of the same name, is one of the shows from the period that epitomized the values of the 1950s and early '60s through the all-American nuclear family. The series stars real-life married couple Ozzie and Harriet Nelson as well as their sons, David and Ricky. The focus of the series is the Nelsons' home life as they deal with run-of-the-mill problems that families of the day faced. By the time the show went off the air, it had produced 435 episodes over 14 seasons.

channel.name: Z Living US
channel.title: The Carol Burnett Show
channel.desc: Comedian and stage actress Carol Burnett, who first gained popularity during her stint on "The Gary Moore Show," hosted this one-hour variety series. Her talented supporting players included Harvey Korman, Tim Conway, Vicki Lawrence (who got the job based on her resemblance to Burnett) and Lyle Waggoner. Skits often featured guest stars, such as Mama Cass of the Mamas and the Papas or singer Steve Lawrence. One sketch, "The Family" (which featured Lawrence as the persnickety Mama and Burnett as her hotheaded daughter) was later spun-off into it's own sitcom.

channel.name: Z Living US
channel.title: The Adventures of Ozzie & Harriet
channel.desc: Long-running sitcom "The Adventures of Ozzie and Harriet," based on a radio show of the same name, is one of the shows from the period that epitomized the values of the 1950s and early '60s through the all-American nuclear family. The series stars real-life married couple Ozzie and Harriet Nelson as well as their sons, David and Ricky. The focus of the series is the Nelsons' home life as they deal with run-of-the-mill problems that families of the day faced. By the time the show went off the air, it had produced 435 episodes over 14 seasons.

channel.name: Z Living US
channel.title: The Carol Burnett Show
channel.desc: Comedian and stage actress Carol Burnett, who first gained popularity during her stint on "The Gary Moore Show," hosted this one-hour variety series. Her talented supporting players included Harvey Korman, Tim Conway, Vicki Lawrence (who got the job based on her resemblance to Burnett) and Lyle Waggoner. Skits often featured guest stars, such as Mama Cass of the Mamas and the Papas or singer Steve Lawrence. One sketch, "The Family" (which featured Lawrence as the persnickety Mama and Burnett as her hotheaded daughter) was later spun-off into it's own sitcom.
